scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I've been living with my parents since I was pretty young, and I'm now 33. I pay them $200 a month, which they say is market rate where we live. I don't see any shame in that because it's super cheap, and I have everything I need without the hassle of finding a new place. We mostly get along, but I try to avoid them as much as possible. Recently, there was a toilet flood in my bathroom, so they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of that, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. Today, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to get up and help them bring in the groceries. I told her I'd do it in a minute. Honestly, I was too into the game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I told him I'd do it in a minute. He said, "A minute is now," grabbed the controller out of my hand, and it turned into a huge shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. Of course, they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They have their golden child, of course, but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean, I guess I could have gotten up and helped them, but to me, because I pay rent, that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yardwork. Am I the asshole in this situation? I'm not sure. Let me think about this step by step. First, I pay rent, which is $200 a month. They say it's market rate, but I'm not sure if that's true. If it's really market rate, then I'm getting a good deal. But if it's below market rate, then maybe I'm taking advantage of them. Second, I've been living with them for a long time, and I'm 33 now. It's unusual for someone my age to still be living with their parents, especially in many cultures. They might feel that I should be more independent. Third, when they asked me to help with the groceries, I was playing a video game and told them I'd do it in a minute. They ended up having to make several trips, and my dad got frustrated enough to take the controller away, leading to a shouting match. Fourth, they're now checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place to live by Friday, which seems unrealistic. Fifth, they brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted. They might be comparing me to him, which is hurtful. So, am I the asshole? Well, I do pay rent, but maybe I'm not contributing enough to the household beyond that. They might feel that I should help out more, especially since I'm living under their roof. On the other hand, I'm an adult, and I pay rent, so I should have some say in how I spend my time. But maybe there's a balance between being independent and contributing to the family. Also, the fact that they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place by Friday seems extreme. It might be a way for them to force me to leave, but it's not very considerate. In terms of the shouting match, I was playing a game, and they were asking for help. I told them I'd do it in a minute, but they ended up having to make multiple trips. Maybe I should have been more considerate of their needs and helped them right away. Overall, I think there's some fault on both sides. I should have been more willing to help out, especially since I'm living with them. But they might also be being too rigid and not understanding my need for independence. I guess the main issue is the balance between contributing to the household and maintaining my independence. If I were to leave, that would solve the problem, but it's not practical to expect me to find a place in just a few days. Maybe I should communicate more openly with them about my needs and theirs. That way, we can find a middle ground where I contribute more, but they also respect my need for independence. In the end, I think I'm not entirely the asshole, but I could have handled the situation better by being more considerate of their needs and communicating more effectively.
